title: Normalized finite coefficient comparison data before compact-support coherence
statement: For schemes T, open immersions $j:X\to Z$ and maps $\varphi:A\to B$ of finite commutative rings, use the fixed-coefficient and intrinsic constant-ring module sheaves [def-weil-extension-by-zero], restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and the ordinary K-injective direct image [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars]. Define sfFixedRestriction as fixed-coefficient restriction. The unique sectionwise identity realization comparison sfRealizationRestriction and its unit/counit inverse square sfInverseRealizationRestriction transport the unit-normalized left-adjoint comparison sfFixedOpenRestriction to sfOpenRestriction. Define sfDerivedImageRestriction to be the specified K-injective-normalized coefficient comparison. For a compactification c of f [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], sfCompactSupportRestriction is the exact derived open square followed by the derived direct-image square. Finally sfCoefficientRestrictionComp is the sectionwise identity coefficient compositor and sfDerivedCoefficientRestrictionComp its exact localization. These are the existing constructions, with no coefficient-composition law for compact support asserted here.

proof.text: Construct the realization comparison from the unique sectionwise linear lift; its inverse is the unit/counit mate. The fixed open comparison is the uniqueness isomorphism of the composite left adjoints. Use the specified K-injective direct-image comparison and paste the two squares.
